teams.replaced_reason: Guardiola announced on 22 May 2026 that he was stepping down after ten years. He said he could not give a specific reason, only that it was his time. His contract ran to 2027 and he agreed to leave 12 months early.

key_choices.text: In August 2026 Maresca said he would wait until the end of the transfer window to finalise his leadership group, and cast doubt on Erling Haaland as captain.
Rúben Dias is the captain in today's line-up against Fulham, which has three changes: Fernández, Cherki and Gvardiol drop to the bench for Bouaddi, O'Reilly and Foden.
Maresca picked out 18-year-old winger Ryan McAidoo as one of preseason's 'real surprises' and said the best thing for him was to stay with the first team.
Maresca said the age of Academy players will not decide selection. He named Kaden Braithwaite, Ryan McAidoo and Floyd Samba as training daily with the first team.
In the opening-day win over Bournemouth, Maresca paired Marc Guéhi with Elliot Anderson in central midfield and left Rayan Cherki out of the starting XI.
Maresca left 19-year-old Ayyoub Bouaddi on the bench for the 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa. He started Bouaddi, Enzo Fernández and Anderson together in midfield the following week against Brighton.

links.text: Maresca succeeds the man he assisted. He was Guardiola's first-team assistant at City in 2022-23, and earlier coached City's Elite Development Squad.

Maresca arrived after leaving Chelsea mid-season. He said the decision to leave was his own and that his resignation opened the path to City. Chelsea said a settlement including compensation was reached with City.
Fulham's line-up includes two City academy graduates, Shea Charles and Oscar Bobb, who were expected to play in midfield and on the right wing.

reviews.author: Steve Douglas
reviews.headline: Man City's 14-year winning run against Fulham is over after draw in Premier League
reviews.quote: City needed a stunning, edge-of-the-area volley by Elliot Anderson in the 57th minute to salvage a point at Etihad Stadium, after Rodrigo Muniz gave Fulham the lead in the 16th.
reviews.point: Douglas says City were poor again and only escaped defeat through Anderson's superb equaliser, with Haaland wasting good chances and having a goal ruled out in contentious circumstances.

title_options: City Had 1.88 xG. Here Is Why It Ended 1-1
Why Maresca's City Could Not Beat Fulham
script.description:
Manchester City 1-1 Fulham at the Etihad, round 11 of the Premier League. Enzo Maresca said before the match that City concede too many goals and that most are avoidable. We follow that one question through the match: Maresca, Erling Haaland and Oscar Bobb, the miss at minute 24, Elliot Anderson's equaliser, and what the expected goals say about the 1-1.

Sources quoted: Yahoo Sports (Football Muse and City Xtra), Sky Sports, a translated AllFootballApp report, Sports Mole and AP (Steve Douglas). Photos from Wikimedia Commons, credited on screen.

Data: FotMob.

shots.text: Three people carry this story. The first is Enzo Maresca. He was Guardiola's assistant in 2022-23, and he took over on 29 June 2026. Sky Sports reports his promise: to do "my job, in the way I want".
The second is Erling Haaland, alone at the top of City's 4-2-3-1. If City are to fix their night, he is the man who must score.
The third is Oscar Bobb. A City academy graduate, he lines up on Fulham's right wing against his old club, as Sports Mole's preview expected. Remember his name. He matters before the half hour.

shots.text: Etihad Stadium. Minute 7. Haaland shoots, blocked. Minute 8, O'Reilly shoots, blocked. Minute 9, a Dias header from a corner goes wide.
Minute 16. Fulham answer, with their first shot. Oscar Bobb makes the pass, and Rodrigo Muniz scores with his right foot, in open play. 0-1.
FotMob's momentum graph has City on top for 60 percent of the first half. Yet at half-time, it is 0-1. City dominate, and they trail.

shots.text: The turning point is a miss. Minute 24. Haaland shoots with his left foot, very close to goal, down the middle. Saved.
Expected goals, or xG, is learned from many past shots: distance, angle, foot or head, and the kind of pass. It tells you how often a shot like that goes in. FotMob puts this one at 0.75.
Three times in four. It is the best chance of the match for either team. Haaland ends with 4 shots worth 1.0 xG in total, and no goal.

shots.text: Just before the hour, City finally score. From a corner, Elliot Anderson hits a right-footed shot from the edge of the area. AP calls it a stunning volley. 1-1.

Then both benches move at minute 70. City bring on Rayan Cherki for Phil Foden; Fulham change two players. FotMob's momentum had City on top for 80 percent of the 15 minutes before, and 20 percent of the 15 after. Both sides changed, so the numbers cannot split the cause. The match tilts toward Fulham, and City never find a second goal.

shots.text: Here is what the scoreline hides. FotMob's numbers give City 1.88 xG, and Fulham 0.72. Whatever Maresca feared at the back, Fulham got little.
So why only one goal? Not the goalkeeper. Bernd Leno's goals prevented figure is below zero, so he did not save Fulham. The cause is simpler. Only 3 of City's 15 shots were on target.

The other 12 were blocked or missed the goal. Two big chances, none scored. Haaland's was saved, and Rúben Dias's header at minute 42 missed the target. The numbers point to shots that never tested the keeper.

shots.text: Steve Douglas of AP writes: "City needed a stunning, edge-of-the-area volley by Elliot Anderson in the 57th minute to salvage a point at Etihad Stadium, after Rodrigo Muniz gave Fulham the lead in the 16th." FotMob agrees on one thing. It rates Anderson 8.1, the highest of any player.
The lowest rating among City's starters is Haaland, on 6.5. His shots explain it: 4 attempts, 1 on target, no goal.
So, did Maresca fix the avoidable goals? Only in part. Fulham got little, yet one shot still went in. We have no post-match words from either coach, so we cannot hear how he read it.

scenes.on_screen: The goal he asked to avoid

shots.text: Maresca asked for fewer avoidable goals. His defence gave Fulham 5 shots, and one of them, rated at only 0.14 xG, was enough. Muniz's finish was well placed. It still came from a small chance.
At the other end, City's 1.88 xG produced one goal. In our reading, the back did enough and the front did not finish. AP reports that City's 14-year winning run against Fulham is over.
So here is the question for the comments. Was Muniz's goal an avoidable goal, or just football? Tell us below. And if you like football told as a story, subscribe.

notes: Scene 1 opens with 'Etihad Stadium, Manchester. Round 11 of the Premier League.', a label, not a human situation. Open with Maresca sitting in Guardiola's seat and his own words, 'We are conceding too many goals', then ask whether he can fix it.
Scene 1 ends on 'who really controlled this match?', but the finale asks 'a bad day at the finish, or a pattern?'. Pick one open question and answer it explicitly in scene 8 or 9.

Scene 2 spends time on form lines and absences ('Abdukodir Khusanov was a doubt, but he starts', 'Fulham miss Emile Smith Rowe'). Cut to one line and keep Maresca's quote and Arbeloa's 'not relevant' as the stakes.

Scene 3, 'Three people, one afternoon', promises three characters but delivers Maresca, Haaland and Bobb as caption-style intros. Tie each to the story: Haaland is the man who must score, Bobb is the old City academy graduate who sets up the goal.

Scene 7 stacks xGOT, blocks, channel share and a 20,000-run simulation in a few lines. Drop the channel percentage and the blocks hedge ('The numbers cannot say where those blocks happened'), and keep one clear cause: shots blocked or off target, not saved.

The scene 9 lesson ('Chances are not goals', 'Check where shots go') reads like a stats report and repeats the point of scene 7. Replace it with a human payoff: Maresca asked for fewer avoidable goals, yet Fulham scored from a 0.14 xG shot and City's 1.88 xG yielded one goal.

shorts.title: Elliot Anderson: City's best-rated player vs Fulham

shots.text: Elliot Anderson had the highest rating of the match: 8.1. He scored City's only goal.
His goal came from a corner situation. The shot was worth just 0.04 expected goals, so a very small chance. AP called it a stunning, edge-of-the-area volley.
He also took 4 shots, created 3 chances and completed 47 of 51 passes. He won 8 duels and lost 9, so it was not a flawless night.
Erling Haaland had 4 shots worth 1.00 expected goals and did not score. City's best-rated player was a midfielder, not the striker.
Was Anderson the right man of the match? Tell us in the comments. Full story on the channel.

shorts.title: City 1-1 Fulham: better chances, fewer goals

shots.text: City created 1.88 expected goals. Fulham created 0.72. Expected goals, or xG, rates each shot by how often it usually scores.
City took 15 shots, and 3 were on target. Fulham took 5, and 4 were on target.
City had 2 chances worth 0.3 xG or more, and scored from neither. Overall they finished 0.89 goals below what their chances suggest.
Replay these chances 20,000 times and City win 70%, draw 20%, Fulham win 9%. This draw was the less likely result.
The numbers show the gap. They cannot show whether the cause was shooting, defending or luck. City earned more, and converted less. Do you blame the finishing or the luck? Full story on the channel.
